The Admitting Officer

Emergency Hospital

Comment [OET1]: Department

Newtown Hospital

13/09/14

Dear Doctor,

Comment [OET2]: OET prefers: Dear
Admitting Officer,

Re: Ms Sally McConville, aged 38

I am writing to urgently refer the above patient, who has been diagnosed with acute asthma with
suspected pneumonia. She requires your immediate assessment and management.

Comment [OET3]: indentation is not wrong
but it is preferable to omit it

Comment [OET4]: Ms McConville: it is
preferable to name the patient

Today, Ms McConville presented with worsening shortness of breath despite using the previously
prescribed medications. Her vital signs were raised, and she was found to be febrile and using her
accessory muscles while breathing. On examination, widespread wheezing and bi-basal crepitations were
persistent. Consequently, she was commenced on salbutamol nebulization 5mg; however, it did not
improve her condition.

Initially, on 10/09/14, she visited the hospital with clinical features of an infective exacerbation of her
asthma secondary to a viral upper respiratory tract infection. Subsequently, 2 days later, she presented
with a 1-day history of exertional shortness of breath and wheezing, accompanied by a fever and
yellowish sputum. On her chest auscultation, widespread wheezing was heard. As such, amoxicillin
500mg, three times a day and prednisolone 25mg, once a day for 3 days were prescribed. Additionally,
she was advised to continue using fluticasone 250, 2 puffs daily with Ventolin, 2 puffs 4 hourly.

Regarding her medical history, she has asthma, hypertension and depression for which she takes ramipril,
paroxetine, fluticasone and salbutamol, 2 puffs as required, respectively.

[It would be greatly appreciated if you could] carry out further assessment and management of suspected
pneumonia of this patient.

Comment [OET5]: this is not clear to the
reader you are confusing him as you never
mentioned anything about these medications.

Comment [OET6]: pulse and respiratory
rate: not all vitals were raised.

Comment [OET7]: do not put comma after
and if the two fragments are related and the
fragment before it is short

Comment [OET8]: used: use the past to
report vital signs and lab results

Comment [OET9]: Ms McConville: do not
start the paragraph with she/he

Comment [OET10]: it is preferable to write
the numbers from 1 to 10 in words

Comment [OET11]: Thus,

Comment [OET12]: This is not respectively

Comment [OET13]: Ms Mcconville: don’t
use patient you should use the name more

If you have any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Comment [OET14]: faithfully,

Doctor
